name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle018
definition_title: Parameter initialization, prime chains, and compact reporting primitives
natural_language_statement:
The library defines concrete programs for testing an original-position triple, decoding radix digits, initializing all integer parameters, executing a contracting prime chain, deciding a retained reporting leaf, constructing sorted band headers, preparing residue buckets, building trimmed source tables, testing independent row flags, and performing a compact subset-zeta coordinate pass. An original triple test decodes three physical indices and returns true precisely for three distinct indices whose original integer values sum to zero. Radix decoding writes digits in forward, big-endian order while dividing the running quotient through a verified helper.

Given input length $n$, the parameter initializer constructs the block schedule, local graph parameters, selected prime and cap, global output count, radix, rounded band size, and prime window. Its placement record identifies every helper in a fixed finite program. A prime-chain level runs an explicit minimum-score search and multiplies the current modulus by the selected prime. Sorted-band data specify a strictly increasing list with the original value membership, its length, its band count, and its endpoint arrays. Source flags independently test the two orientations against actual retained bucket counts. A compact zeta pass enumerates each required cardinality layer rather than all numeric masks.

The associated invariants, memory predicates, local-mask interfaces, mass scales, and output-record interfaces connect these programs to the finite objects used in the deterministic integer 3SUM proof. Runtime and resource claims are established by the dependent theorems.

name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle019
definition_title: Global keys, retained zeta stages, and physical reporting batches
natural_language_statement:
This library defines the next executable assembly layer: candidate-band rows, original-index band rows, truncated band-length queries, global output-key construction, header-driven owner tables, local cover-matrix construction, original-triple fallback scans, output-record decoding, terminal reporting batches, occurrence-vector arrays, and independent source trimming. It also specifies block source endpoint bounds and the retained compact zeta-stage tables.

For subset width $L$ and cardinality cutoff $c$, the zeta-stage constructor stores all $L+1$ stages in consecutive compact tables with stride $\operatorname{downsetCap}(L,c)$. Its loop invariant preserves every completed stage and restricts changes to the designated destination and scratch regions. The global-key builder constructs the actual output-mask layer, all local keys, and their full positional product from selected coefficient rows. A terminal batch reads the endpoint and independent-flag arrays for each retained candidate, evaluates the physical bucket-pair test, and accumulates a Boolean disjunction. Source trimming multiplies separately computed left and right Boolean flags across selected blocks. The finite fallback scans original triples using the explicit single-triple test.

These definitions retain physical indices and actual stored arrays throughout the deterministic integer 3SUM construction. They provide the exact program texts and loop invariants needed to charge successful reporting work by the sum of physical fiber costs and to reuse the finite library without enumeration assumptions.
